reviews.text: Zack Gottsagen is warm and hilarious as Zak. His personality dominates the screen. Likewise, LeBeouf feeds into Gottsagen’s charm and plays Tyler as understated and confident.
reviews.author: Max Greene

reviews.text: The cast are on their A game, with what could be my favorite performance from Shia LaBeouf and Dakota Johnson. But the reason to see this film is for Zach Gottsagen’s lead performance.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: Shia LaBeouf shines as the angst-ridden antihero. He fully inhabits the character of Tyler, handling crab nets like a pro – the byproduct of crabbing for an entire month prior to filming.
reviews.author: Paul Kanieski

reviews.text: A tender and often funny heartwarmer with loads of charm, personality, and humanity.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: The importance of the family you make, rather than the one you're given, is at the heart of this low-budget independent American feature that just happens to have two enormous Hollywood names on the marquee.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon makes a strong case for the value of sentimentality.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: It might be pretty optimistic in its wholesomeness, but whats the point of the movies if they cant be? Especially in a film that is committed to its faithful and hopeful representation for a  community that is almost never shown on screen whatsoever.
reviews.author: Daisy Leigh-Phippard

reviews.text: Peanut Butter Falcon excels as a story of simple kindness.
reviews.author: Hosea Rupprecht

reviews.text: Swept up in those bayou waters, we all root for Zack and happily accept whatever good fortune the writers provide for him.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: One of the year's biggest and most welcome surprises.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: Far from its tale of friendship and personal growth, 'The Peanut Butter Falcon' is an adventure comedy that is too condescending in tone for my taste. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: What becomes very clear as the film goes along, however, is the lack of experience of the filmmakers. The lead duo meet up with other characters at random, with little or no connection between how any of them got to that particular place.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: One thing it's not, mercifully in this day and age, is cynical.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: An uplifting movie without a bit of cynicism that (as the title might suggest) isn't afraid to be sweetly silly at times.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: A Southern fairy tale that takes the familiar and imbues it with 21st century life ... The simple story, the flawed characters, the highly fantastical and often mythicized location work together to produce a film that is beautiful in its smallness.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Too breezy and unreal to have any lasting impact.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: This is one of LaBeouf's most authentic roles, creating a realistic yet flawed character with a heart and a troubled past.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Simply wonderful.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: While LaBeouf earned an Independent Spirit nod for his turn in American Honey, it's his work here that is easily the best of his career.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Zach Gottsagen plays a young man with Down Syndrome who dreams of becoming a pro wrestler, joining a drifter (Shia LaBeouf) for a Mark Twain journey down south.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: A beautiful, sentimental journey of self-discovery.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Knows what it is, and it embraces every grain of sugar along the way.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: Although the film mainlines The Adventures of Tom Sawyer author's gung-ho spirit and snappy humour, The Peanut Butter Falcon has its own wild heart. A feel-good film with soul, it has a lot to say about how we look at people with disability
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: You'd have to be made of iron not to be affected by The Peanut Butter Falcon and its lazy raft of delights.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: It adds up to a climax that . . . ropes in its subplots in hopes to tying everything together. But this isn't a tale that should weave smoothly. It's a folktale.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: It exudes an innocence, kindness, and optimism that is unusual in contemporary independent cinema, which is usually much more tragic. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Desirée De Fez

reviews.text: Excellent chemistry between the amazing Zack Gottsagen and Shia LaBeouf. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Cortijo

reviews.text: The whole thing is just so damn sweet that I couldn't help but feel uplifted. Add to that a handful of genuine belly laughs and you've got yourself a winner.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: A small and bittersweet indie that succeeds...
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a sweet, tender and joyful portrayal of an unlikely friendship, and it won't fail to charm.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: It's elevated beyond cloying corniness by the naturalness of its performances, from Zack Gottsagen's unstoppable energy to Shia LaBeouf's quiet warmth and crushed-but-not-broken spirit.
reviews.author: Laura Di Girolamo

reviews.text: Gottsagen's performance shows that a disabled actor can still have the range that an able-bodied actor can have and still have the presence to drive a film all by themselves. Hopefully other film makers will take notice and follow suit.
reviews.author: Joel Fisher

reviews.text: And although essentially a fable, the film reminds us that the world is a complicated place and none of us are in any position to judge someone solely on their appearance or past actions - as tempting as that often might be.
reviews.author: Steven Sheehan

reviews.text: What follows could be a bit corny. Indeed it is a bit corny, and that is part of its charm. Life is a bit corny too.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: This dédebutbut feature from Tyler Nilson and Michael Schwartz is built upon a wonderfully naturalistic performance by Zack Gottsagen...
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: There isn't a literal 'peanut butter falcon' in The Peanut Butter Falcon, but true to the title, it's a sticky-sweet film that soars on the strength of its easy-breezy cast.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: For a screen newcomer, Zack Gottsagen turns out to be a real find. Far from just showing up and saying his lines, Gottsagen closely collaborated with the filmmakers in filling out and sharpening his character.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: It's impossible to think of another actor who could pair desperation, care and naked compassion in the way that LaBeouf delivers in this film.
reviews.author: Blake Howard

reviews.text: The rough-edged charm of this redneck reworking of Mark Twain's Huckleberry Finn radiates from the beautiful, warm performance by Zack Gottsagen...The unforced, uplifting vibe of the film makes it easy to understand its status as a sleeper hit.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Picturesque, soul-warming cinema that proves representation in cinema regarding talent with a disability can be possible without reducing them to a stereotype.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: A simple tale told impeccably well, 'The Peanut Butter Falcon' proves you don't need a lot of flash to land a mighty impact.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: As calculated as the film might be, it's hard to dislike. And while Nilson and Schwartz use Gottsagen's sincerity as a guarantee of their own good intentions, this never feels as exploitative as it might have.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: A mixed set of square pegs becomes a force to be reckoned with.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: ...a parable on the outsider, with a lot of healthy rumination of disability in the mix, but like the best efforts, it doesn't make a big show of 'daring to talk about it'.
reviews.author: Cain Noble-Davies

reviews.text: Writer-directors Tyler Nilson and Michael Schwartz have crafted a very pleasing movie that is funny, touching and somewhat uplifting. Too often, we forget there are a lot of good people in the world. This is a movie that celebrates good people.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Representation for people with genetic disorders still has a long way to go, but this is the rare film that seems to be moving the needle instead of placating the masses.
reviews.author: Michael Snydel

reviews.text: LeBeouf's casting was inspired, because his chemistry with Gottsagen lights up the screen and LeBeouf, who has always been a good actor who made bad choices, gets the chance to really show what he can do.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: If you are looking for a feel-good film that lauds the overdue representation of humankind in all its shapes and forms, The Peanut Butter Falcon is the way to go.
reviews.author: Lydia Gan

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a rambling, ramshackle comedy-drama that like the makeshift boat at the centre of the film, should not float, but does so anyway.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: One of those almost tactile films where you can nearly touch and smell and feel everything on screen - the courageous intimacy feeds an understated narrative, giving room for the performances to drive home the emotion.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is an absolute gem.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: An undeniably cheerful feature. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: You have to be made out of stone to be unmoved by The Peanut Butter Falcon.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: It succeeds despite its flaws, at least, in being zany, lightweight and crowd-pleasing entertainment.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: [The] pitch-perfect casting and rustic setting lend its familiar tale an edginess that somehow both offsets and enhances its inherent sweetness.
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: There's a lot of subtlety where backstory is concerned and plenty of heart for the present. A lot of this is due to the genuine rapport between LaBeouf and Gottsagen.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Talk about a feel good movie! The Peanut Butter Falcon will warm your heart, time and time again.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: ...a mostly compelling little drama...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The whimsy lapses into sentimentality in places, and Dakota Johnson is sold somewhat short as Zak's compassionate carer. But her rapport with Gottsagen is as effective as LaBeouf's, while Nigel Bluck's widescreen waterscapes are sublime.
reviews.author: David Parkinson

reviews.text: You know where you are, you can feel the location...really atmospheric with a lovely story.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a charming movie, filled with humanity and heart, even if it doesn't always make narrative sense.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: Slightly overcooked but very sweet.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: [LaBeouf's] harmonious connection with Gottsagen pretty much comprises the entire film, but such is the relaxed timbre established by Nilson and Schwartz, you're happy to hang out with them.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Perhaps against the odds, this shambling buddy movie really works.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Like a Disney family drama from TV times past, this feelgood road movie is so homely, so warm and fuzzy, and so darn wholesome that it's almost too much.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: It's a step forward that the directors cast an actor with disabilities rather than getting a star to "crip up". But it's a long way from making a film which creates a complex, genuine three-dimensional portrait of life with Down's Syndrome.
reviews.author: Saskia Baron

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon isn't shy of pushing your buttons, but the overall effect has an innocent charm and frankness, and LaBeouf brings a winning combination of toughness and soul.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: This indie charmer may operate on familiar ground but it's big on heart and driven by great performances. What's more, it even manages to avoid some fairly obvious clichés to deliver surprising but subtle emotional depth and even a little darkness.
reviews.author: Rob Carnevale

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon gets two cheers... for its redemptive warmth and a troupe of actors unfailingly bringing out the best in each other.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: LaBeouf is scruffily compelling, while the pinpoint comic timing of Gottsagen should be a lesson to any drab corners of the film industry still resisting disabled actors.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: A featherweight film with a lot of heart but not much staying power.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: This is LaBeouf at his best, stripped down to his bare elements and bookended by two luminous performances from Gottsagen and Johnson.
reviews.author: Beth Webb

reviews.text: Gottsagen is endearingly funny and LaBeouf once again nails it as an appealing scruffbag. Together, they're a cockle-warming delight.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is better than it has any right to be, the potential mawkishness of its premise offset by its acuity for local detail.
reviews.author: Thomas Atkinson

reviews.text: The relationship between LaBeouf and Gottsagen is the film's backbone, both narratively and emotionally. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: A charming and engaging drama with a light comedic edge.
reviews.author: Rob Aldam

reviews.text: Its message of autonomy and risk-taking is infused with a sense of magic as Zak, Tyler and Eleanor drift through the stultifyingly hot river-ways of the American South. And rather than leave its characters enervated it says that anything is possible.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a life-affirming odyssey with an incredible dynamic between the lead actors.
reviews.author: Adam Solomons

reviews.text: An uncommonly earnest and warm-hearted film that doesn't condescend its under-represented subject - or the audience.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is beautiful, sentimental and oh, so sweet.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: With heart, laughs and one of the purest on-screen friendships this year, it is hard not to fall in love with The Peanut Butter Falcon.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon takes viewers on an adventure. It makes us think, and it makes us feel. If you're like me, you'll laugh, you'll cry and you'll be glad you took a chance on a Shia LaBeouf movie.
reviews.author: Amanda Greever

reviews.text: A seemingly mismatched road-trip buddy movie, Tyler Nilson and Michael Schwartz's The Peanut Butter Falcon is heartwarming and filled to the brim with humour and charm.
reviews.author: Zoe Margolis

reviews.text: A pleasant, heartwarming story, that includes Shia LaBeouf's best performance to date. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: A heartfelt story about people rediscovering their own self-worth and, in seeing themselves through another's eyes, learning the value they still have to offer the world.
reviews.author: Adam Lubitow

reviews.text: Two people from opposite ends of the spectrum and they find common ground for friendship. That's what it is all about. People need people.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: A heartwarming buddy comedy, The Peanut Butter Falcon is a modest film that is filled with emotion, humour, and empathy with charming performances across the board.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: This story of a man with Downs Syndrome going after his dream of being a wrestler was inspired by the main actor's dream to star in a film. The mess of a script failed to maintain momentum but the actors managed to deliver some feel good moments.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: LaBeouf is excellent but the film's treatment of Gottsagen's Zak and the buddy-buddy relationship between the two leads. The Falcon is a breath of fresh air in an otherwise dour late summer film landscape.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: The performances were great, the writing is really clever and really funny and really cute.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: An inspiring and touching adventure about discovering our inner strength and learning from each other's differences. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Thanks to an endlessly entertaining screenplay and an incredible performance fromShia LeBeouf,The Peanut Butter Falconrises above the crop.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: In the moment of watching it, nothing ever feels like it has any kind of urgency, anything that propels it forward.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: If our humanity is going to be restored, fostered and buttressed, it's art like this that will accomplish the deed, by reminding us all what it means to believe in one another.
reviews.author: Rick Levin

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a small movie with a big beating heart.
reviews.author: Chase Whale

reviews.text: 'Peanut Butter Falcon' is sweet-natured tale of friendship, freedom
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: I hope the people who hate those with Down syndrome see this movie so they can see how wrong they are and become nicer.
reviews.author: Nathanael Hood

reviews.text: This is a rare movie that is sincere, joyous, and un-cynical, but also artfully made ... In dark and anxious times, we need more films like this.
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: This may have as much to do with the colorful eastern seaboard settings as it does the filmmakers' sensitive handling of the main character's developmental disability; the film feels authentic as well as sincere.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon might not be a perfect movie, but it is certainly a worthwhile one ... a film driven by humor and heart.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: It sounds syrupy, well intentioned but clueless, and riddled with potentially problematic characterization. Yet somehow FALCON largely dodges the entire minefield it seems barreling towards.
reviews.author: Tim Stevens

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a film that understands, and teaches us, that in order to thrive we must spend time working to understand those around us.
reviews.author: Melissa Sloter

reviews.text: Raw and unrefined, The Peanut Butter Falcon is a testament to the power of independent filmmaking.....Gottsagen steals scene after scene...
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: Directors Tyler Nilson and Mike Schwartz have made their feature debut with intelligence, warmth, and nuance.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Dakota Johnson is superior to her reputation, and sustained work in indie efforts will bear that out. As for Shia LaBeouf, he has never been better in a movie.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: When you name your movie "The Peanut Butter Falcon" (Zak's planned wrestling name, by the way), you are announcing that you're a quirky indie. But the joys this movie brings will stick to the roof of your mouth.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: What separates this movie from the rest in its category are the buoyant performances. LaBeouf and Gottsagen have a natural chemistry, which helps us care about their travels toward freedom.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a distinctly American fable of resilience and perseverance that's nothing less than wonderful, this marvelous riverboat journey one I am not soon to forget.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon borders on surreal fantasy. That it works at all is amazing; that it works as wonderfully as it does is miraculous.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is at its best when it simply lets the unlikely, touching friendship at its center unfold.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: There are moments where it strains credibility a bit... but the movie has such a great feeling of true happiness and the characters are so well realized and so well performed that you kind of over look it.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: Peanut Butter Falcon 's a feel-good movie in every sense of the word, driven by stellar performances. But most importantly, we get a hero whose community isn't represented enough in films - and the few times they are, it's stereotypical.
reviews.author: Joi Childs

reviews.text: LaBeouf's dangerous, rough-hewn charm gives Tyler a compelling edge; he remains one of the most commanding actors of his generation, and he's reason enough to buy into the tale.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Inspiring, feel-good film.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: A feel-good end to the Summer.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: The movie occasionally falls prey to early filmmaker mistakes, but its winning performances and its delightful star are more than enough to buoy it along.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a heartwarming movie that soars in so many ways.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Icky, sticky title and all, this 'Falcon' still flies mostly toward the heart, with a fine cast and story that remains enjoyable along its improbable way.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Endlessly charming thanks to the terrific chemistry between LaBeouf and Gottsagen, a bonafide find by the writing-directing team of Tyler Nilson and Michael Schwartz.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: At its best this big-hearted picture recalls the setting, and feeling, of Jeff Nichols' Huck Finn-indebted coming-of-age fable "Mud."
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: This is exactly the kind of movie we need right now. Sadly, those who need to see it most, likely won't.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: The film's reality-defying, storybook approach to the plot and the characters grows on you.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Touching and genuine, a modern Tom Sawyer tale without a hint of blackheart irony. Nice to see Shia LaBeouf as an actor rather than a performance artist.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: It's difficult to turn a blind eye to some of the creative lapses on display here, but come on, I'm not made of stone, and against all odds, this fitfully winning crowd-pleaser wore down my defenses. It lets kindness lead the way.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Dramatically speaking, it's a little lightweight, but the chemistry between [Zack] Gottsagen and [Shia] LaBeouf is pro-level rapport.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: It is timeless and a triumph.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Writer-directors Tyler Nilson and Michael Schwartz team up to bring you what is quite possibly the feel-good movie of the year, for good and ill.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: This is one of [Shia] LaBeouf's most authentic roles, creating a realistic yet flawed character with a heart and a troubled past.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is sweet without piling on the saccharine and a tremendous story about pain, acceptance and how both can lead to growth.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Funny and charming, with a central trio of appealing performances. A pleasant distraction from present-day tensions.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: What it lacks in originality, it makes up for in refreshingly empathetic charm.
reviews.author: Barry Paris

reviews.text: A sweet story of friendship that has an old school southern charm about it. "Falcon" is easy to watch and really easy to like.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Corniness aside, The Peanut Butter Falcon is good-looking with a solid ensemble cast and a legitimately inspiring message.
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a tender and simple drama about finding your strength, with a deceptively nuanced performance by LaBeouf, who continues to be one of the most compelling actors working today.
reviews.author: Julie Crawford

reviews.text: If you're predicting that these two men will forge an unlikely but close bond, you may have seen an independent movie before. However, the familiarity of "Falcon" doesn't make the journey any less sweet.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: ...once the credits roll you won't feel very good about having spent the last 90 minutes with these characters and receiving such little pay-off.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: ...easily one of the most-rewarding viewing experiences you are likely to have at the theater this year.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The chemistry between Shia LaBeouf and Zack Gottsagen is tender and charming. Tyler may not be the perfect guardian for this young man, but their bonding is irresistibly heartwarming
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Exactly as predictable as you expect & you love it exactly as much as you expect. And that's a lot. Fun flick & the kind that gets awards. Or at least is nominated for them.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: Life might be imitating art or vice versa, who knows? One thing is certain: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a wonderful piece of art.
reviews.author: Stephen Rodrick

reviews.text: The performances are lovely, and there's plenty of pleasant moments ... if that's enough for you to overlook a swamp full of other flaws, have at it.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Here's a film that feels both like a fable and quite authentic.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The inspired combination of Shia LaBeouf's Tyler and Zack Gottsagen's Zak is a strong candidate for Onscreen Duo of the Year.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Impressive performances lend credibility to this fanciful journey.
reviews.author: Roger Tennis

reviews.text: A generally amiable tale of runaways and redemption...the visual storytelling here offers a raft of subtle pleasures.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: An endearing friendship, folk tale, that's so lite-hearted, it's also forgettable.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: The film has a central character, who's not only appealing on an essential story level, but he's also so utterly different from what we're used to seeing on-screen that much of what we encounter is a crowd-pleasing revelation.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: It's a rare example of a comfort food level crowd pleaser with a great deal of ambition to go along with its hard earned uplift.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: We can see the full picture clearly, too - so much so, finally, that this easygoing odyssey offers no real surprises.
reviews.author: Tom Russo

reviews.text: Peanut Butter Falcon, the story of a fugitive on the lam with a young man with Down syndrome, is an affecting, appealing piece of Americana.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Falcon morphs from a charming, funny parable about overcoming one's disabilities to a large helping of southern-fried ridiculousness.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: The movie is too convoluted to really make a point.
reviews.author: Hannah Lynn

reviews.text: Teeming with personality, emotion, and engaging characterizations, with the helmers successfully riding the fine line between saccharine and sincere.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The chemistry between Tyler and Elenor is magnetic. It was actually so good it made me wish Dakota Johnson and Shia LaBeouf would get together in real life.
reviews.author: Katrina Olson

reviews.text: A lucky penny of a movie, a beacon of unfiltered goodness that never forgets that the number one rule of happiness in life is to party with the people you love.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: The film is a sweet, funny and heartfelt look at friendship and strength.
reviews.author: Samantha Incorvaia

reviews.text: Shia Le Beouf is at his emotional best. As his character regains his humanity, he becomes the heart of the film. Zack Gottsagen as Zak is the soul.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Gottsagen is the ultimate Method actor. He doesn't "inhabit" the role, because for him, it's not a role. He literally IS the man determined to overcome an obstacle, and he's amazingly honest and wonderful in doing it.
reviews.author: Chuck Yarborough

reviews.text: You can guess what is going to happen in this odd-couple-buddy-road-trip movie that touches all the necessary points but does it in a likable, good-hearted manner that has you rooting...all the way through.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: undeniably sweet, a little corny and often laugh-out-loud funny...Gottsagen and LaBeouf fall into a wonderful rhythm, a pair of odd couple coconspirators on a distinctly regional American adventure.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: A small film with a big heart.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Bolstered with Gottsagen's natural sweetness, and advancing with a favorable propulsive élan, The Peanut Butter Falcon mixes cliched narrative with feel-good energy.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The kind of experience that makes one rethink how their own story is going.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: The film is sweet but it's Zack Gottsagen's inclusivity that makes it truly special.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: In a time of rampant cynicism The Peanut Butter Falcon dares to offer a sweet, sincere story with a happy ending. No wonder audiences are responding to it.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: A tender story that is enhanced by the wonderful performance of Zack Gottsagen. It touches your heart but never reaches the magical level it should have.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a quiet film at times, yet thanks to gorgeous cinematography and incredible performances from the two lead actors, it's never boring.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: Though this is a formula picture that occasionally ventures into hokey territory (notably in its climactic moments), it's engaging and warm throughout.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: It is a bit gooshy, with a baptism by a profane junkyard reverend and a magical realist moment of triumph. Still, the Outer Banks waterscapes make The Peanut Butter Falcon funky and appealingly summery.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: "The Peanut Butter Falcon" is a nice little movie that barely goes anywhere, but audiences, in a certain mood, might be willing to drift along with it.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: ...it's the film's charismatic newcomer Zack Gottsagen who emerges as a champion.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: [T]he film's on-the nose allusions to Twain ultimately contribute to a sense of derivation, undermining the originality of the material and preventing "Falcon" from graduating from good to great.
reviews.author: Travis DeShong

reviews.text: This movie is one heaping dose of kindness and support.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Hands down the best film of 2019 so far. If you see any movie this summer, make it "The Peanut Butter Falcon."
reviews.author: Kaely Monahan

reviews.text: It is lovely, funny, and never condescending.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a little movie which is showing some real legs. A small labor of love, the film steps out from behind the often formulaic tropes of its genre to make a powerful statement about not only character, but family.
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: With the film's gently loping pace and rather obvious villainous subplot, there's a sense that it was made up as the cast and crew went along. This adds an improvisational charm to the story, even as it twists through some rather predictable beats.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: LaBeouf brings the soul to "The Peanut Butter Falcon," while Gottsagen brings the spirit. He has an undeniably charming screen presence, and the actor takes to this starring role with gusto.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: A heartwarming, tender and funny adventure grounded in humanism. Refreshingly witty and unconventional. It's one of the summer's best surprises.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is, seemingly by design, a rather small film, which works perfectly when it's trying to be the gentle hangout movie that it mostly is.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: Stick around for the third act...I loved Thomas Haden Church in this...but it's very derivative.
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: While you've seen all this, I like the relationship and the casting in this movie. And I loved that ending. It's not a disappointment if you go see this.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Shia LaBeouf and Zack Gottsagen make the perfect pair to go on the lam in this engaging Mark Twain-ish adventure that flows as smoothly as the river it takes place around.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon saves the worst for last, as the plot kicks into gear during the third act and blunts the film's delicate emotional texture into a contrived drumbeat of dull choices.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: A beautiful story about human connection, heroes, and finding the joy of simply living your truth.
reviews.author: Yolanda Machado

reviews.text: The two stars convey a charming chemistry that smooths out the rough patches in the screenplay, and helps this road movie take flight.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Shia LaBeouf and newcomer Zach Gottsagen make this buddy movie one for the ages.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: The total mix adds up to a kind and heartwarming movie about human relationships, and "The Peanut Butter Falcon" should provide a nice escape for audiences weary of our conflicted social media driven culture.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: "The Peanut Butter Falcon" tells one of those delightfully old-fashioned stories where friendships are formed on the run. It's about outcasts and dreamers, told with a simplicity that proves you don't need a massive budget to say something meaningful.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: It is a small, lovely work with excellent, all-in performances from Gottsagen and especially LaBeouf, who is becoming a more interesting and nuanced actor as he gets older.
reviews.author: Joe Gross

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a film that could have easily been written by the likes of Mark Twain if the author lived during this era.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Peanut Butter Falcon, which avoids gooey sentiment, takes its fanciful title from the name Zak chooses for his wrestling alter ego. The title proves suggestive; this is a movie that isn't afraid of its sometimes goofy appeal.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: THE PEANUT BUTTER FALCON is a very sweet movie. It certainly has a distinctly goofy charm.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: It is remarkably assured for a first film, with an excellent supporting cast of talented pros and superb cinematography and music choices.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: This lovely debut feature by Tyler Nilson and Michael Schwartz trafficks in the pleasure of watching intriguing people working through outlandish problems in unlikely ways. Go in expecting the best and you'll come out smiling.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon may lack depth and subtlety, but you can always feel the beat of its heart.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: While "Falcon" occasionally feels a bit too ramshackle along its lead characters' journey, it still arrives at a destination that's more than satisfying.
reviews.author: Carl Kozlowski

reviews.text: Gottsagen is a disarming performer who creates a sweet and funny character.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: The screenplay by Tyler Nilson and Michael Schwartz (also the directors) cuts deep. Between the fun interactions of its characters are quiet nuggets of wisdom and truth. Let it carry you to happiness.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: This weird concoction somehow works, thanks in no small part to the acting chops of Shia LaBeouf and the charm of newcomer Zack Gottsagen.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: What's clear is that a lot of development time, movie resources, and A-List actors all came together to make a masterpiece of a film centering on one person...Zack Gottsagen.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: Sure, Scarlett Johansson could probably have played the role (as well as any of the trees in the background). But if you seek a good example of why diversity in casting and conception makes for a richer cinema landscape, look no further.
reviews.author: Mike D'Angelo

reviews.text: Hopeful movies like this are just what we need right now.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Though the plot of this mismatched-buddies drama may feel overly familiar, the bold casting and watery setting provide a welcome edginess that enhances the inevitable sweetness, making it genuine.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: It is an infinitely sweet indie that wears its Mark Twain inspiration on its sleeve just as readily as the cardboard box that makes up the wrestling gear.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: Terrific - a low-key charmer and one of the most accessible indie films of the year.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: A very enjoyable film that might have some appeal to wrestling fans
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: "The Peanut Butter Falcon" is a fantastic fairy tale of a film. Truly a wonderful/crowd pleasing experience. An absolute delight from start to finish, it's among 2019's best.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: It's an impossibly sweet meditation on what it means to be a hero and empower those around you. With a free-spirited adventure story and the most heartwarming performances of the year, The Peanut Butter Falcon soars.
reviews.author: Brent Goldman

reviews.text: ... The Peanut Butter Falcon, a film which wears its heart on its sleeve without an ounce of sarcasm or cynicism. In many ways, The Peanut Butter Falcon is too pure, making it the perfect salve for the rancor permeating our lives today.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a sweet, warm story about dreams and the family you choose. Zack Gottsagen is pure comedy. Shia LaBeof is giving me sexy, scruffy with substance and the pairing of these two on screen is perfection.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: The film's improvisational feel helps to ground a fable-esque narrative in a discernible reality.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: Anchored by two strong performances from Shia LaBeouf and newcomer Zach Gottsagen, "The Peanut Butter Falcon" - though following a familiar path - finds salvation in its picturesque worldview of reality while offering a rousing look at life.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: It's one of those movies that captures a sense of time and place very well and we enjoy spending time with these characters.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon is a beautifully uplifting tale of humanity and friendship. It's a true crowd-pleaser from start to finish. Shia LaBeouf's range in this performance is remarkable.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Fueled by LaBeouf and Gottsagen's screen chemistry, The Peanut Butter Falcon makes for a charmingly funny and often touching adventure.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: A well-told story with unexpected heart to match, The Peanut Butter Falcon swoops in and charms your pants off.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: "The Peanut Butter Falcon" is an uproarious, odd-couple buddy flick that is laced with so many laugh-out-loud moments.
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon may not reinvent the wheel, but the relationship at the core of the film and the stellar performances by LaBeouf and Gottsagen will melt your heart.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: As we go on this journey, it's easy to settle into the dangerous yet relaxing vibes of the deep south. At the end of the tunnel is a romanticism for life, to drink it all in with a smile on your face and to expect the impossible.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: By keeping the humor rooted in the performances and only letting sentimentality creep in when necessary, Nelson and Schwartz have crafted a film that feels refreshing, unique, and emotional.
reviews.author: Ryan Oliver

reviews.text: The Peanut Butter Falcon's tale traverses a well-worn foundation, but this riff on the road movie is both distinctly modern and bracingly optimistic.
reviews.author: Randall Colburn

reviews.text: Logic is sometimes sacrificed in the name of friendship in The Peanut Butter Falcon, an American odyssey with a welcomed retro feel and a good heart where its lead duo can romp in cheery harmony.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: LaBeouf holds the screen with natural allure, making every twinge of his character's self-reproach, and every instant of his dawning joy, achingly felt. His nuanced performance propels this journey.
reviews.author: Sheri Linden

reviews.text: A feel-good niche indie with its priorities in the right place.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

synopsis: After running away from a residential nursing home to pursue his dream of becoming a pro wrestler, a man who has Down syndrome befriends an outlaw who becomes his coach and ally.
